result.summary:
Scope test: YES, real user-visible/behavioral surface (three new live Telegram commands /staff_add, /staff_remove, /checkin that mutate event_staff and audit_log, and refuse/authorize live callers) -- full Steps 3b/4 apply. Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-018.md covering AC1-AC6 plus the SECURITY-REVIEWER Step 2c addition (treated as AC7: audit_log row on every /checkin refusal branch). Read apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaff.ts, eventStaffAuthorization.ts, handlers/staff.ts, handlers/checkin.ts, docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md, the existing unit tests (eventStaff.test.ts, eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts), the live i18n catalogs (types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts staff.*/checkin.* blocks), index.ts's three command registrations, and handlers/venue.ts + handlers/event.ts (confirmed real exported handler names makeVenueNewHandler/makeEventPublishHandler and venue.createUsage's real multi-line body format and both handlers' shared venue.notAuthorized/event.notAuthorized string 'You are not authorized to do this.' for AC2's dispatch). Reused REQ-013/014/015/016/017's established grammY-dispatch harness convention (real bot.handleUpdate() against real fixture Postgres, tg_id range 1000000100+ to avoid collision with prior specs) -- never a mocked Context, per REQ-013's established defect class to avoid.

Gaps found in BACKEND-DEV's existing unit tests (both files are real and already passing, not duplicated -- named per-case which existing test to re-run as a live-integration cross-check instead): (1) eventStaff.test.ts only covers parseStaffCommandArgs -- no unit coverage exists (nor should it, DB-dependent) for getEventStaffRow/addEventStaff/removeEventStaff's actual INSERT/DELETE + exactly-one-audit-row transaction shape, or for the new domain/user.ts addition getUserByTgUsername -- AC5 closes this with live audit_log row-count checks across assign/remove/duplicate-assign/remove-never-staffed. (2) eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts's checkEventStaffAuthorization/buildCheckinRefusalAudit cases all pass hand-built ActingUser/EventStaffRow/Date objects directly -- no test proves getEventStaffRow's real SQL correctly scopes by event id (AC1's live cross-event case closes this), that a real Postgres timestamptz column round-trips into the endsAt comparison correctly (AC3's live case), or that requireEventStaffForEvent's composed entry point actually calls writeAuditLog on all three refusal reasons against a live DB and never on success (AC7a-d closes this -- this is the exact S5 security-rework regression class from commit 15b6ec2 that has zero live-DB coverage today). (3) Neither unit test file, nor any existing test, dispatches through handlers/staff.ts or handlers/checkin.ts at all -- so the full handler composition (argument parsing, organizer-gate-before-target-lookup ordering, already-assigned/not-assigned pre-checks, and critically the notification recipient/language selection for AC4) is entirely uncovered until this spec's live dispatches. (4) AC2's two named organizer-only surfaces (/venue_new, /event_publish) have never been dispatched against by any EventStaff-only caller in any prior spec -- REQ-015/016/017's own specs test these handlers' organizer gate against plain members and organizers, never against a user who additionally holds an event_staff row, which is exactly the confusion AC2/design-§0.4 exist to rule out. Did not write a case for AC2's third named surface ('registration list') per the task's explicit instruction -- confirmed via git grep that no such handler exists in this codebase yet (design §6.5), consistent with the design gate's prior acceptance of this as a structurally-guaranteed-but-not-yet-testable surface.

Every AC has >=1 case that would fail if the corresponding behavior were wrong; each case states its failure mode. Also added AC-schema (git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db empty, confirming the design's own 'no schema change' claim) and AC-catalog (i18n key parity for the 11 staff.* / 4 checkin.* keys across types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts, plus the three index.ts command registrations) as mechanical checks, matching REQ-017's spec's own convention of separating dispatch cases from static/grep checks.
